doc_verification.detail: Reachability: WebFetch to api.qdrant.tech was blocked by the sandbox domain policy, but a live fetch via the web-reader tool returned the full page (canonical URL https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/indexes/create-field-index, Fern-rendered, fetched 2026-09-03) — recorded as PASS, not domain_blocked, because content was actually retrieved. Version: page route v-1-18-x and selector show v1.18.x, matching target 1.18.0 (major.minor equal). Content: the page Body declares 'field_schema (enum or object or object or object or object or object or object or object or object or any, optional)' — a union of one string-enum and 9 object variants plus a rendering-artifact 'any'; NO sequence/array form is declared anywhere on the page, and the page's own cURL example uses the string form "field_schema": "keyword". Nuance: the Fern page collapses the enum member list inline; the assertion's 8 members {keyword, integer, float, geo, text, bool, datetime, uuid} match the source enum PayloadSchemaType (lib/segment/src/types.rs:2155-2164) exactly. Endpoint: endpoint_registry entry 'index+create PUT' with this exact source_url; the doc page is 'Create payload index' PUT /collections/{collection_name}/index; the tested request used that same face (field_name in body). Page is the REST API reference (SDK snippets only demonstrate the string form), so no SDK/REST confusion.

secondary_observations: rest same-parameter control (output_semantic_index_create_002.log:6): [PUT index sic025ff4dd_live/ctrl_ok] schema="keyword" -> status=200 raw={"result":{"operation_id":2,"status":"completed"},"status":"ok","time":0.3236951} — positive face healthy (G4 ground)

rest same-parameter contrast (output_semantic_index_create_002.log:7): [PUT index sic025ff4dd_live/h_int] schema=123 -> status=400 raw={"status":{"error":"Format error in JSON body: data did not match any variant of untagged enum PayloadFieldSchema at line 1 column 44"},"time":0.0} — scalar shape rejected

rest same-parameter contrast (output_semantic_index_create_002.log:8): [PUT index sic025ff4dd_live/h_bool] schema=true -> status=400 raw={"status":{"error":"Format error in JSON body: data did not match any variant of untagged enum PayloadFieldSchema at line 1 column 46"},"time":0.0} — boolean shape rejected

rest same-parameter array-length contrast, cross-script (output_boundary_index_create_004.log:11): [probe field_schema [] (array shape)] body={"field_name": "m_arr_schema", "field_schema": []} -> status=400 raw={"status":{"error":"Format error in JSON body: data did not match any variant of untagged enum PayloadFieldSchema at line 1 column 50"},"time":0.0} — EMPTY array rejected while the 1-element array ["keyword"] was accepted: the positional-seq signature, not blanket array leniency

rest same-family parameter (untagged-enum leniency family, output_boundary_aliases_update_002.log:36-37): probe[double-key-element] -> status=200 raw={"result":true,"status":"ok","time":0.015951735} — a different serde untagged enum (AliasOperations) silently accepting an invalid element shape in the same run; distinct defect_id, cited as family context

grpc face (source-grounded, not live-probed — live cross-face probe unobtainable: sandbox exposes REST only, face_unavailable recorded): lib/api/src/grpc/qdrant.rs:5528 declares field_type: Option<i32> #[prost(enumeration = "FieldType")] — the gRPC face is a plain protobuf enum and structurally cannot carry a JSON array, so this acceptance is REST/serde-specific

http_semantics.note: A request-side-decidable type error (field_schema as JSON array, a shape outside the documented union) was answered HTTP 200 with a full success envelope ({"result":{"operation_id":4,"status":"completed"},"status":"ok"}) — not merely a 2xx with an error code but a pure success acknowledgment, i.e. complete silent acceptance; sibling shapes 123/true/[] show the server DOES use 400 + serde diagnostic for the same parameter, so the 200 is not a blanket 2xx policy

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: field_schema IN {keyword, integer, float, geo, text, bool, datetime, uuid}; text tokenizer IN {prefix, whitespace, word, multilingual}
contract_grounding.note: The observed parameter IS field_schema and the observed value ["keyword"] is a JSON array — not a member of the asserted string-enum domain, and not the object-with-type branch either (endpoint request_required_paths = [field_name, field_schema.type]). The semantic value ('keyword') being legal does not cure the violation: the doc declares only enum/object wire shapes for field_schema, and the undocumented array form was silently coerced into the object branch (source shows it deserializes positionally into KeywordIndexParams). Violates-declaration self-check resolved as 'genuinely a domain violation' — the constraint citation is the correct one.

chain_links: contract: qdrant_type_index_create_001 exists in structured_contract.json type_constraints (endpoint index+create, evidence_tier explicit, source_url https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/indexes/create-field-index); request_required_paths=[field_name, field_schema.type]
doc: live-fetched v-1-18-x create-field-index page declares field_schema as enum-or-objects union with no array form; cURL example uses string form "keyword"

script: semantic_index_create_002.py put_index() sends body {"field_name": "h_arr", "field_schema": ["keyword"]} via runtime path_key create_index with wait=true — raw request targets exactly the constraint's parameter

log: output_semantic_index_create_002.log:9 records schema=["keyword"] -> status=200 with completed operation envelope; control "keyword"->200 and 123/true->400 bracket the behavior; VERDICT line 10-11 matches the raw response
chain_trace.note: Minor dispatch-metadata gap, not a chain break: the candidates.jsonl entry for this defect_id carries constraint_id="" (truncated attack string), but the attack string names constraints::qdrant_type_index_create_001 and the executed script header declares '# constraint_ids: qdrant_type_index_create_001'; the id resolves uniquely in structured_contract.json.

files_examined: lib/segment/src/types.rs (lines 2140-2330: PayloadSchemaType / PayloadSchemaParams / PayloadFieldSchema; lines 4995-5025: test_payload_parsing)
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: PUT /collections/{name}/index (update_api.rs:374) -> Json<CreateFieldIndex> (update.rs:303) -> field_schema: Option<PayloadFieldSchema>, untagged (types.rs:2276) -> variant FieldParams(PayloadSchemaParams), untagged (types.rs:2188) -> Keyword(KeywordIndexParams) — serde's derived struct deserializer accepts the JSON SEQUENCE form positionally (visit_seq): ["keyword"] fills field 0 r#type=KeywordIndexType::Keyword and #[serde(default)] fills is_tenant/on_disk/enable_hnsw, so the array silently deserializes into the object branch; Validate (types.rs:2302) then passes trivially. The empty array [] fails because field 0 has no default (invalid_length), producing the observed 400 in boundary_index_create_004 — the positional-seq signature. Scalars 123/true match neither variant (not a string, not a map/seq) -> the observed untagged-enum 400s. No comment, doc line, or test declares array acceptance: test_payload_parsing (types.rs:5012-5025) covers only the string form and object serialization; the line-21 comment in index.rs explains the type-field design was chosen 'for OpenAPI schema without anonymous types, versus #[serde(tag = "type")]' — an OpenAPI-schema motive, not an intent to accept arrays.
source_grounding.outcome_note: validation_absent (not by_design_in_source): the contract-required shape validation — field_schema must arrive as the documented string-enum or object-with-type form — is not enforced on the REST face; the array acceptance is an unannotated side effect of serde's positional struct deserialization interacting with the untagged enums and #[serde(default)] trailing fields. Bare silent behavior with no explicit design declaration cannot be marked by_design per the v3.4 tightening; the only design comment found (index.rs:21) concerns OpenAPI schema shape, not input leniency. The gRPC face (prost enum, qdrant.rs:5528) structurally cannot accept an array, so the leniency is REST-specific.

excluded: request-parameter typo / client-side marshalling (the runtime printed the exact body it sent — json.dumps of the same variable put into the request; the sibling 400s returned serde errors at columns 44/46 that byte-match the sent bodies {"field_name": "h_int", "field_schema": 123} / {"field_name": "h_bool", "field_schema": true}, proving faithful transport)
environment problem (control leg 200 with completed operation; deterministic deserialization-layer behavior, not infra flakiness)

concurrency / cache delay (single-threaded request sequence; the phenomenon is request-shape-decidable and reproduces the source-predicted split: [] rejected vs ["keyword"] accepted across two independent scripts in the same session)
